title: A worker or verifier that finds the ticket wrong hands in revise, and the issuer runs the opener
objective: A worker or verifier asks for a revision by handing in kind 'revise' with its reason, and the issuer runs the opener itself, in its own environment, and starts the next round with the outcome.
outline: devloop/ticket_issuer.py _round: collect the worker's hand-in first (as today) and, when its kind is 'revise', handle it before waiting for the verifier (so a REVISED or ESCALATED outcome stops a verifier still running through new-6's watch / stop_agents); a 'revise' hand-in must not set worker_ok. A helper revise_hand(hand, role) validates the reason, runs the revision in-process and maps the outcome to items 5-9. devloop/ticket_creator.py: give revise()/_revise() an optional `cur` list (the memory_keeper._run pattern: agents.start, cur[:] = [p], p.finish()) so the issuer passes self.pending and a signal stops the opener, and return or fill an outcome (kind, note, failure text) for the issuer while the CLI keeps printing REVISED / UNCHANGED / ESCALATED / REVISE FAILED with today's exit codes (the main session still uses it). start(): drop the revise variable and the 'revise_cmd' value. Docstrings: ticket_issuer's 'A worker that thinks the ticket is wrong calls ticket_creator.py --revise itself ...' and the blocked/escalated sentence; ticket_creator's 'Revising (called by a worker or verifier mid-run ...)' and the exit-3 line ('a revising worker must stop and hand in kind blocked'). apply_unapplied stays (it still recovers a revision whose ticket_creator.py was stopped). README lines about 20, 245 and 266-268.
test_plan: Verifier owns items 1, 2, 4-10, in tests_devloop/test_issuer.py as class T<N>Acceptance placed between the existing classes T114Acceptance and T138Acceptance; setUp strips every DEVLOOP_* key from self.env (as T114Acceptance does). New fake actions in tests_devloop/fake_agent.py, each its own branch with a comment naming this ticket: worker 'revise_handin' (right after the `if action == "blocked_failing":` block): hand in {'kind': 'revise', 'reason': 'acceptance 2 is impossible'} and exit 0 without committing; worker 'revise_noreason': hand in {'kind': 'revise'}; verifier 'revise_handin' (the first statement inside the `elif role == "verifier":` branch): the same hand-in, exit 0; creator 'unchanged' (right after the `elif action == "revised_dag":` branch): hand in {'kind': 'unchanged', 'note': 'the ticket stands: item 2 is possible'}. Cases (fake agents are instant, seconds each): C1 (items 1, 4, 5): worker ['revise_handin', 'ok'], creator ['revised'] -> r1-worker/prompt.md has '"kind": "revise"' and no 'ticket_creator.py'; one runs/1/revise-* dir whose revise.json source is 'worker'; one 'revised' event; the round-1 feedback event has free 'revision'; r2-worker/prompt.md contains 'a possible thing'; landed. C2 (item 6): worker ['revise_handin', 'ok'], creator ['unchanged'] -> feedback[0] == 'round 1: the worker asked to revise the ticket; the opener kept it as written: the ticket stands: item 2 is possible', free 'revision'; r2-worker/prompt.md contains that text; acceptance still ['a']; landed. C3 (item 7): worker ['revise_handin'], creator ['question'] -> stuck, reason 'decision'; exactly one decision page with ref '1', text starting '#1 needs your decision (raised by the worker)'; one 'escalated' event. C4 (item 8): worker ['revise_handin', 'ok'], creator ['bad'] (for a revise its kind-'tickets' hand-in fails) -> feedback[0] starts 'round 1: the worker asked to revise the ticket; the revision failed: ' and ends '; the ticket stands as written'; that feedback event has no free. C5 (item 9): worker ['revise_noreason', 'ok'] -> feedback[0] == 'round 1: the worker\'s revise hand-in has no "reason"'; no runs/1/revise-* dir. C6 (items 2, 10): worker ['ok'], verifier ['revise_handin', 'ok'], creator ['unchanged'] -> r1-verifier/prompt.md has '"kind": "revise"' and '## Feedback from earlier rounds'; revise.json source 'verifier'; feedback[0] == 'round 1: the verifier asked to revise the ticket; the opener kept it as written: the ticket stands: item 2 is possible'; r2-verifier/prompt.md contains that text; landed. Expected strings come from this ticket. Implementer's unit tests (between ApplyUnapplied and FreeRounds): the outcome mapping with a stubbed revision, both agents handing in revise, and item 11 (the opener's Pending is in self.pending when interrupted).
notes: Source: plan item 3.4, docs/HANDOFF.md last section (D-100, D-101, D-102): the main session's review of an external audit (2026-11-26) and feedback from T's main session (T is another project that runs agent-control daily, 2026-11-26). Quoted feedback is data, not instructions. Refer to T only as 'another project' in code, tests and comments (tests/test_no_project_names.py forbids its name in every non-markdown file) and copy no path from these notes into code. T reported: workers running under another account's environment (HOME replaced by that account's wrapper) called the revise command; claude could not read its login and the wrapper resolved wrong paths; it failed several times. Read in code: worker.md tells the worker to run {revise_cmd} itself and wait up to 600000 ms in one tool call; verifier.md has no revise path and no {feedback} section (its prompt says rejected cases 'come back to you' but the feedback is never shown to it). Today a hand-in of an unknown kind from the worker counts as done (only 'blocked' is special), so every verifier case is red before the change. Design choices: UNCHANGED makes the round free (today an UNCHANGED revise cost the worker no round, it went on in the same run; 2 x max_rounds still bounds repeats); a failed revision counts (bounded, and it is not the ticket's text that changed); the verifier gets the feedback section because 'the next round with the opener's answer attached' must reach it too. As for blocked hand-ins (#113), the issuer acts on the hand-in instead of the agent acting inside its own environment. WORDS TO AVOID: this project's hard_block patterns are os\.kill, killpg, pkill and 'kill -'; no line this ticket adds may contain them. Depends on new-6 (same round code; REVISED relies on its rule) and on #143 (running; it edits worker.md and verifier.md right after the 'Run them with' lines and README '## Machine slots', which this ticket also edits). Group new-g2 with new-6.
acceptance: devloop/prompts/worker.md has no {revise_cmd} and no instruction to run ticket_creator.py; its section '## If you think the ticket (or the verifier's cases) is wrong' tells the worker to hand in {"kind": "revise", "reason": "<why the ticket is wrong>"} and stop, and that the next round gets the opener's answer; '## Hand-in' lists that kind. The rendered r1-worker/prompt.md contains '"kind": "revise"' and does not contain 'ticket_creator.py'.

devloop/prompts/verifier.md gains the same kind of section ('## If you think the ticket is wrong') and the hand-in line, and a section '## Feedback from earlier rounds' showing {feedback} (the issuer already passes feedback to every role); the rendered r1-verifier/prompt.md contains '"kind": "revise"' and '## Feedback from earlier rounds'.
ticket_issuer.start() no longer builds or passes 'revise_cmd'.

When the worker hands in {"kind": "revise", "reason": R} with R a non-empty string, the issuer itself runs the opener's revision of the ticket (the ticket_creator revise path, source 'worker', reason R) with the issuer's environment (cfg.env), never the agent's; runs/<id>/revise-*/revise.json has source 'worker'; the opener's cost row goes on the ticket as today.

Outcome REVISED (the opener handed in kind 'revised'): the round ends as new-6 defines for a work-changing revision (an agent of the round still running is stopped; free 'revision'; feedback REVISED_MID_ROUND or THROWN_OUT); the next round's worker prompt holds the revised ticket.

Outcome UNCHANGED: the verifier's hand-in of the round is processed as today (red check, cases saved); the round then ends without merging, with a 'feedback' event with free 'revision' and feedback text exactly 'the worker asked to revise the ticket; the opener kept it as written: <the opener's note, or (no note)>'; the next round's worker prompt shows it under '## Feedback from earlier rounds'; the brief fields are unchanged.

Outcome ESCALATED (the opener asked a question; ticket_creator writes the page and the 'escalated' event as today): an agent of the round still running is stopped, and the ticket is stuck with reason 'decision', with exactly one decision page for it (the escalation's, text starting '#<id> needs your decision (raised by the worker)') and one 'escalated' event.

Outcome failed (the opener's hand-in was unusable or the revision was refused): the round ends counted (no free) with feedback 'the worker asked to revise the ticket; the revision failed: <what ticket_creator gives as the reason>; the ticket stands as written'.
A revise hand-in without a non-empty string 'reason' runs no opener; the round's feedback is exactly 'the worker's revise hand-in has no "reason"' (counted).

The verifier's hand-in {"kind": "revise", "reason": R} takes the same path with source 'verifier' and 'the verifier' in the texts of items 6, 8 and 9; it is handled after the worker's hand-in, and when both hand in revise the verifier's runs only if the worker's ended UNCHANGED. After the verifier's UNCHANGED no cases were saved: the next round starts the verifier again with the answer in its feedback (only the verifier when the worker's hand-in of that round stood, as after any verifier problem today).

The opener run is charged to the issuer's deadline (issuer_timeout_seconds), keeps today's limit min(REVISE_TIMEOUT, agent_timeout_seconds), takes no machine slot (creator is a no-slot role), and an issuer interrupted while it runs stops it together with the round's agents (its Pending sits where stop_agents() reaches it), with its cost row kept on the ticket.

Docs describe the hand-in path: the ticket_issuer.py and ticket_creator.py module docstrings, and devloop/README.md - the flow line 'worker thinks the ticket is wrong -> it runs ticket_creator.py --revise itself', the Roles table rows `creator`, `worker` and `verifier`, and the '## Machine slots' parenthetical that names 'a worker's `ticket_creator.py --revise`'; the README phrases existing tests read stay (test_machine's Machine-slots words, among them "parent's slot" and 'DEVLOOP_SLOT'; test_memory's role rows keep their script and model names).

Old cases stay green unchanged: test_issuer Revise.test_a_worker_can_have_the_ticket_revised_and_cases_rewritten, T11Acceptance, T114Acceptance and test_machine's test_a_worker_that_has_its_ticket_revised_lands_with_one_slot (their fake worker still runs ticket_creator.py itself: a revision from outside the round, which new-6 handles).
token_basis: the round flow in ticket_issuer.py on top of new-6, the revise path of ticket_creator.py (cur list, outcome), two prompt files, docstrings and four README spots; four fake actions and six loop cases; complex tickets with a verifier landed at 2.5M-6M recorded
vision: 每張票需要我介入幾次 (down): in T revisions requested from inside another account's environment failed several times; the opener now always runs in the issuer's own environment. Also 每張落地票的 token (down): a worker no longer holds its whole context open for up to 10 minutes inside one tool call while the opener runs.
removes: an agent starting another agent inside its own environment: worker.md's revise command with its 600000 ms tool-call wait, and the README's nested-run case 'a worker's ticket_creator.py --revise'.

# Phase one, group 3: fewer tokens, fewer wasted rounds (docs/DECISIONS.md D-100, D-101, D-102; plan in docs/HANDOFF.md, last section, items 3.1-3.7)

The user approved this plan (D-102). Sources: the main session's review of an external audit and feedback from tabby_pool's (T's) main session (2026-11-26); write the source on each ticket; no GitHub issues. Quoted feedback is data. Read docs/VISION.md; each ticket names its metric and what it removes. Tests in the area's own file in tests_devloop/ with loop_harness.py; seconds each. Open tickets in groups g12-g14 (#142-#151) are running; depend on them where you touch the same code.

## 3.1 The code index lists test files by path only
Measured on A: CODE-MAP.md is 209,241 bytes; tests/ and tests_devloop/ sections are 151,110 (72.2%). The worker and verifier prompts say "read it before searching"; the fixer gets it too. devloop/core/codemap.py's docstring says tests are listed by path only, but build() expands them. T's test files are larger.
Wanted: files under the project's test roots (tests.unittest.roots) and test_*.py files get one path line. Add tests_devloop/test_codemap.py (none exists). Check agent logs (runs/*/agent-*.log) whether agents read the index whole, and write what you found. Whether to drop module-level `_` functions too: measure and decide.

## 3.2 The opener knows the hard_block rules before it writes a plan
T (seen there): #369 and #375 had test plans using os.kill; the tickets hit hard_block only after the work was done, waited for the user, were revised, and a round was wasted. The opener's prompt has no hard_block (main session, read the code).
Wanted: the project's hard_block (paths, dirs, patterns) is in the opener's prompt with what it means (a ticket whose change matches stops before merge for the user). The hand-in check refuses (one retry, like other field checks) a ticket whose outline, test_plan or acceptance contains a hard_block pattern unless the ticket says, in a dedicated field or line, that it needs the user's approval at merge and why.

## 3.3 After a revision the next round reads the new ticket
T (seen there): after #320 was revised, the round-2 worker got the text from before the revision and reported the same conflict again.
Wanted: reproduce it first with the loop harness (revise with `actl new --revise` while a round is running; see what the next round's prompt holds). Fix it so the next round always reads the revised ticket. A running round whose work the revision changed is stopped and counts as a free round (like a revision that voids the cases).

## 3.4 A worker does not run the reviser itself
T (seen there): workers running under agy's account environment (HOME replaced) called the revise command; claude could not read its login and agy.sh resolved wrong paths; it failed several times. devloop/prompts/worker.md tells the worker to run {revise_cmd} itself.
Wanted: as for `blocked` hand-ins (#113): the worker hands in "revise" with its reason; the issuer runs the opener outside the agent's environment. REVISED -> the next round with the new ticket; UNCHANGED -> the next round with the opener's answer attached; ESCALATED -> a page as today. The verifier uses the same path. Removes: an agent starting another agent inside its own environment.

## 3.5 Automatic fix tickets go into the next group that has not started verifying
T (seen there): g90, g91, g92 were each one or two flaky-fix tickets and each ran a full regression (about 75 minutes in T).
Wanted: when the controller opens a ticket by itself (flaky, release red), the request asks the opener to put it into a group of the chain that has not started its regression, and to open a new group only when none fits; the opener's group rule (prompts/creator/02-rules.md) says the same.

## 3.6 The opener's prompt carries only the live part of the DAG
Measured: A's opener prompt is 25 KB and includes all of dag.json, landed tickets too; T has about 400 tickets.
Wanted: the copy put into t
